title: Forensic validation sweep for customer FP8->INT8 exception
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer (large financial institution) opened a support ticket requesting an exception to allow FP8-like fast paths on their latency-sensitive endpoint. They reported a 1.8% accuracy drop when switching from our standard INT8 profile to the requested FP8-compatible runtime on their regulatory inference workload. They require a forensic calibration run + targeted validation sweep to: reproduce the regression, determine if a bespoke calibration profile can recover accuracy within SLA, and produce artifacts for approvals (legal/compliance + model governance).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Reproduce customer-reported accuracy delta on a held-out subset with the same input distribution. 2) Identify a calibration/quant profile that reduces the accuracy regression to <=0.5% absolute difference vs baseline INT8. 3) Produce a reproducible runbook and a validation report (metrics, diffs, trobleshooting notes) signed off by Applied ML and Support. 4) If no profile meets threshold, provide recommended mitigations (fallback policies, latency/accuracy trade-off) and a customer communication draft.
plan_steps: Obtain customer sample set + data schema; validate PII/contract permissions
Create isolated env with customer's model variant and matching runtime (runtime-1.22)
Run baseline INT8 calibration to generate reference metrics (perplexity, F1/accuracy depending on task)
Run FP8-compatible fast path with existing generic calibration profile to reproduce regression
Iterate calibration grid (scale, clip, per-channel vs per-tensor) to find candidate profiles
Perform targeted A/B evaluation on stratified slices (numeric stability, long-tail prompts)
If candidate found, run stress test with load + latency SLO check and record KV cache behavior
Draft validation report, include PRs, notebooks, and S3 artifacts; route to Applied ML + Support for sign-off
Coordinate customer communication and optional production rollout plan (canary, monitored rollouts)
run_results_summary: Preliminary forensic run on 2026-03-03 reproduced a 1.7% absolute drop on the customer sample (N=12k). A calibration grid (12 profiles) produced two promising profiles: Profile-A recovered to 0.6% delta, Profile-B to 0.4% delta but increased tail latency by ~12ms. Additional stability testing required. No numerical instabilities or NaNs observed. Detailed metrics and per-slice breakdowns uploaded to S3 run ID s3://redwood-quant-runs/ENG-31122/2026-03-03/
